12 Entry Points

Diplomatic

1. Diplomatic Network

280+ posts worldwide — embassies, high commissions, consular services, crisis evacuation coordination. Network operations, staffing, security vetting, secure comms infrastructure, host-government liaison, diplomatic bag handling, and visa processing across every continent.

Policy

2. Foreign Policy

Sanctions regimes via OFSI, treaty negotiations, UN/G7/G20 engagement, human rights reporting. Strategic policy development, sanctions design, diplomatic demarches, country policy briefs, and Foreign Secretary advisory pipeline covering 195 nations.

Development

3. Development Aid

ODA budget £12.8bn, FCDO programme delivery, humanitarian response, ICAI oversight, British International Investment (BII). Aid effectiveness measurement, partner country coordination, multilateral disbursement, and results-based financing across 150+ recipient nations.

Trade

4. Trade Policy

FTAs (Australia, Japan, CPTPP), export controls, NSI Act investment screening. Trade barrier resolution, market access negotiation, investor protection, strategic trade licensing for dual-use goods, and WTO dispute settlement coordination.

Security

5. International Security

CSSF conflict stabilisation fund, peacekeeping operations, non-proliferation (NPT/OPCW), cyber diplomacy, maritime security. Counter-terrorism cooperation, arms control verification, security sector reform, and defence engagement across priority regions.

Climate

6. Climate Diplomacy

COP legacy leadership, NDC commitments, loss & damage fund, green finance mobilisation, Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JETPs). Climate vulnerability assessments for ODA recipients, adaptation finance tracking, and Nature-Based Solutions deployment.

Intelligence

7. Open Source Intelligence

Research Analysts network, horizon scanning, OSINT collection, disinformation detection. Fuse open sources across 280+ posts into actionable intelligence for policy and crisis decisions. Includes social media monitoring, satellite imagery analysis, and media monitoring.

Digital

8. Digital & Technology

Virtual embassies, GovTech for development, cyber capacity building, AI governance diplomacy. Digital infrastructure in fragile states, internet freedom, responsible AI international norms, and digital identity for displaced populations.

Identity

9. Passports & Nationality

HMPO operations, British nationality law, Emergency Travel Document (ETD) issuance, fraud detection. Passport processing, citizenship verification, identity management for nationals abroad, and nationality casework for complex heritage claims.

Crisis

10. Crisis Response

Rapid Deployment Team (RDT), consular crisis operations, evacuation planning, COBR coordination. Natural disasters, conflict zones, terrorism events, mass casualty incidents affecting UK nationals, and repatriation logistics for stranded citizens.

Multilateral

11. Multilateral Governance

UN system engagement, Commonwealth coordination, international organisations, multilateral development banks. Voting blocs, leadership bids, assessed contributions, institutional reform advocacy, and treaty body reporting across the multilateral system.

Accountability

12. Parliamentary Accountability

Foreign Affairs Select Committee, FCDO Questions, Freedom of Information requests. Ministerial accountability, NAO audits, ICAI reviews, public transparency obligations, and written ministerial statements on foreign policy decisions.

8 Transformation Priorities

Priority 1

Diplomatic Network Digitalisation

Consular case processing 15→5 days, visa backlog reduction -60%. Unified case management across 280+ posts with automated document verification, appointment scheduling, and status tracking. Target: 85% digital-first consular journeys by 2027.

Priority 2

Sanctions Enforcement Intelligence

Evasion detection 35%→85%, OFSI licence processing 8wk→2wk. AI-powered beneficial ownership tracing, transaction monitoring, and network analysis across UK financial system. Target: 95% sanctions list coverage with <24h update latency.

Priority 3

Development Aid Optimisation

Programme evaluation 18mo→6mo, diversion detection >99%. Satellite imagery, financial flow analysis, and ground-truth verification for ODA disbursement. Target: real-time aid impact dashboard across all FCDO bilateral programmes.

Priority 4

Conflict Early Warning System

Prediction accuracy >75%, lead time 3mo→9mo. Multi-source fusion of OSINT, satellite, economic indicators, and social media for conflict risk assessment. Target: automated risk scores for all 280+ post countries updated weekly.

Priority 5

Trade Intelligence Platform

Trade barrier identification 6mo→4wk, export licence processing 60d→15d. Automated FTA compliance monitoring, market opportunity detection, and dual-use goods screening. Target: 100% FTA tariff schedule coverage with daily change detection.

Priority 6

Climate Diplomacy Dashboard

NDC assessment frequency annual→quarterly, green finance tracking 100%. Climate vulnerability scoring, JETP progress monitoring, and loss & damage fund disbursement tracking. Target: real-time climate finance flow visibility across all ODA partners.

Priority 7

Consular Crisis AI Assistant

Response activation 4h→30min, mass notification 2h→15min. Automated crisis detection, British national location tracking (opt-in), and evacuation route optimisation. Target: 95% of crisis-affected nationals contacted within 30 minutes.

Priority 8

Diplomatic Cyber Defence

Vulnerability detection 30d→24h, data spillage detection 100%. Continuous monitoring of diplomatic networks, secure comms verification, and insider threat detection across all posts. Target: zero successful state-actor breaches of FCDO classified systems.

⛔ 6 Sovereign Red Lines

  • 🚫 No sanctions imposed without explicit FCDO Secretary of State approval — automated list addition is prohibited.
  • 🚫 No diplomatic communication intercepted, stored, or analysed by AI without Foreign Secretary authorisation.
  • 🚫 No development aid allocation decided solely by algorithm — human programme director sign-off required.
  • 🚫 No British national data shared with foreign intelligence services without judicial warrant.
  • 🚫 No evacuation order issued by automated system — requires human crisis centre director authorisation.
  • 🚫 No trade deal terms negotiated by AI — requires Trade Secretary explicit authorisation for any commitment.

5-Step Engagement Model

1
Discovery
Map FCDO estate — 280+ posts, ODA programmes, sanctions workflows, crisis protocols. Identify AI-ready processes and sovereignty constraints across diplomatic, development, and security pillars.
2
Governance Design
Deploy DORADO patterns — constitutional red lines, bilateral protocol guardrails, and multilateral compliance gates. Align with Article 50, Vienna Convention, and data protection across jurisdictions.
3
Pilot
Launch controlled pilots in consular case management, sanctions monitoring, and OSINT fusion. Measure against KPIs: case time reduction, evasion detection rates, crisis response activation speed.
4
Scale
Roll out proven MCPs across all 280+ posts. Integrate with FCO corporate systems, COBR, OFSI, HMPO. Deploy sovereign OWEM adapters for diplomatic and development domain specialisation.
5
Assure
Continuous sovereignty verification — Article 50 compliance, red line enforcement, parliamentary accountability. ICAI audit trails, NAO integration, and Foreign Affairs Committee reporting.
